facts.claim: On the fourteenth of August Arjun wrote to the Ardent Ridge team at partners@ardentridge.test that Nimbus Labs is raising a seed round, and asked for twenty minutes.
That mail to partners@ardentridge.test bounced as soon as it was sent.
The partners' address is the only address the file holds for Ardent Ridge, and no person there is named.
The file still names the move as theirs; the engine filed it as an investor relationship under fundraising.

inferences.claim: Ardent Ridge never received the pitch, so nothing is in its hands: the move the file gives it is not the fund's to make.
Any silence from Ardent Ridge says nothing about its interest — it has nothing to answer.

hypotheses.proposition: The address or the fund's domain was mistyped.
hypotheses.needs: The bounce report's own reason, and the address on the fund's site.

hypotheses.proposition: Ardent Ridge takes pitches only through a named partner or an introduction.
hypotheses.needs: The fund's site, or someone who knows its partners.

unknowns.question: Why the mail bounced — the file records only that it did.
unknowns.relevance: A typo is fixed by resending; a dead address needs another way in, such as an introduction.

unknowns.question: Who the partners at Ardent Ridge are, and whether the fund invests at seed in this space.
unknowns.relevance: A named partner's address beats a shared box; a poor fit makes the resend not worth the time.

frames.primary: A pitch that never arrived: the mail to Ardent Ridge bounced, so the fund has nothing to answer and the next move is the founder's.
rivals: A typo in the address, fixed by resending to the right one.
A fund with no working shared address, where only an introduction to a partner gets in.

proposed_kind.why: Arjun pitched Nimbus Labs' seed round to the Ardent Ridge team, and the engine already treats the file as an investor relationship.

expected_vs_actual.expected: Without a playbook, a pitch that arrives waits on the fund's answer.
expected_vs_actual.actual: The pitch never arrived: it bounced, so there is nothing for Ardent Ridge to answer.

scenarios.do_nothing: Ardent Ridge never hears of Nimbus Labs, and the file sits as if the fund were deciding.
scenarios.act: A working address, ideally a named partner's, puts the pitch in front of the fund while the seed round is still open.
scenarios.best: The resent pitch lands with a partner who asks for a call.
scenarios.worst: No working address turns up, and the fund stays out of reach without an introduction.
signals_to_watch: A second bounce from the new address.
An answer from Ardent Ridge once the pitch arrives.
Someone in the founder's network who knows an Ardent Ridge partner.

reasons: Raising the seed round is the brief's first goal, and this fund never saw the pitch.
Finding the right address costs little and can be done at once.
A resend can go out at any time; a wrong guess costs only another bounce.

next_move.what: Find a working address for Ardent Ridge — read the bounce report for its reason, check the fund's site for a named partner — and resend the pitch there.

answer.alternative: If no working address turns up, ask someone who knows an Ardent Ridge partner for an introduction.
answer.wait_or_stop: Nothing to wait for: the fund never got the mail. If a second address bounces too, stop writing cold and look for an introduction.
answer.done_when: The pitch reaches someone at Ardent Ridge without bouncing.
answer.draft: Hello, my note to the Ardent Ridge partners' address bounced, so I am resending it here. Nimbus Labs is raising a seed round. Could we find twenty minutes to talk? Arjun
